profile.reading: This is one of eleven OpenStreetMap points sharing the identical name Blockfusion Niagra Falls, all located at or near 5380 Frontier Avenue in Niagara Falls, New York, most plausibly representing separate structures within a single campus operated by BlockFusion USA, Inc. rather than eleven genuinely distinct facilities. BlockFusion, founded in 2019 by CEO Alex Martini-Lo Manto and COO Kant Trivedi, converted a retired coal-burning power plant at this address into a cryptocurrency mining hosting campus that is increasingly pivoting toward artificial intelligence and high-performance-computing colocation. The site draws roughly 90 percent of its power from carbon-free hydroelectric generation supplied by the nearby Robert Moses Niagara Hydroelectric Power Station, according to a 2022 SEC filing by hosting customer Bit Digital, Inc., a publicly traded Bitcoin mining company. A second major customer, Gryphon Digital Mining, Inc., signed a colocation agreement effective December 1, 2024, hosting nearly 5,000 mining machines on 12 megawatts of power. As of BlockFusion's most recent disclosures, the campus has 46 megawatts of Tier 1 power currently energized, with more than 100 additional megawatts of Tier 3 capacity planned as part of an AI and HPC-focused expansion developed with architecture and engineering firms Gensler, JB&B, and Thornton Tomasetti. In November 2025, BlockFusion announced plans to go public through a merger with special-purpose acquisition company Blue Acquisition Corp, becoming Blockfusion Data Centers, Inc. under ticker BLDC, in a deal valuing the company at 450 million dollars pre-money, a transaction still pending as of the most recent regulatory filing found. The underlying colocation contract with Gryphon describes the site as including both mobile container-based mining units and indoor pod space within larger main buildings, a documented, phased-construction pattern that plausibly explains why multiple separate structures were mapped at this one campus rather than indicating genuinely distinct facilities.

reading.body:
BlockFusion's Niagara Falls campus currently operates 46 megawatts of IT capacity with plans to expand to over 100 megawatts, making it the second-largest facility by published capacity in New York State, though the state overall has published specifications for only 3 megawatts across mapped data centers. The site has converted a retired coal power plant into a colocation facility drawing approximately 90 percent of its power from the nearby Robert Moses Niagara Hydroelectric Power Station, qualifying it to serve customers seeking carbon-free infrastructure for compute-intensive workloads. The operator, founded in 2019 and currently pursuing a public merger, has documented colocation agreements with cryptocurrency mining operators and is developing additional capacity specifically for artificial intelligence and high-performance computing alongside its existing mining hosting business.

At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, the current 46 megawatts of IT load represents roughly 1,150 racks, with the planned 100-megawatt expansion potentially reaching approximately 2,500 racks. The campus comprises 11 mapped structures at a single address, representing separate buildings within one campus rather than distinct facilities, which explains why published capacity for this one operator exceeds the total for all other mapped facilities in the state. No information is published on which specific artificial intelligence workloads or tenants currently occupy the site, pricing, or grid interconnection details beyond the stated hydroelectric sourcing.

The facility sits in New York State alongside 30 other mapped data center locations, only one of which has published megawatt specifications beyond this campus. The pending merger values BlockFusion at 450 million dollars pre-money and would list it under ticker BLDC, a transaction still awaiting regulatory approval as of the latest filing. The site's leverage of existing industrial power infrastructure and hydroelectric generation, combined with its stated AI and HPC expansion plans, positions it to scale materially in the near term if the merger closes and additional capacity comes online.
